chapter: Lessons, WPA band and sidemen years
title: The WPA band and the Fifth Ward Club
summary: Morgan played in the WPA band of about 119 players, rehearsing at the Fifth Ward Club on Dumaine Street.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: No, no. Somebody else told me that. The only band, a big band that I played in around that neighborhood, well we used to go and rehearse, so every day that was the WPA band.
Well, you were in the WPA band?
Yeah, I played in the WPA band. You might have seen one of my, seen my pictures.
Yes, I've seen those pictures. Yeah.
Well we had from close around 119. About everybody in town was in that.
Yeah. I don't know who was in the picture, but I remember an awful lot of people.

Well I stayed, I stayed in that band until we cut the band on to 19 pieces at that time. Now we used to rehearse over at the Tulane's Club, and we used to rehearse a lot here on, about the Fifth Ward Club out here on Dumaine Street.
Yeah, somebody told us, I know Kid Clayton told me they worked over there. I never knew that.
Yeah, just on Dumaine near Charter Street. Near Charter, is that what even? Between Charter and Decatur.
What sort of a place was it then?
Well it used to be a, Atlanta club, you know, boxing and different things. Oh yeah. Yeah. They called that the Fifth Ward Club. Yeah.
It's not there now I guess then.
Well that was during the WPA time.
